newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL REGAIN PRIDE BUT PSG BATTLE TO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL REGAIN PRIDE BUT PSG BATTLE TO FINAL.

text.p: Holders Paris Saint Germain lost 2-0 to a rampant Liverpool but clung on for a 3-2 aggregate victory to earn a place in the final of the European Cup Winners Cup for the second successive season on Thursday.

They will now attempt to become the first club in the competition's 36-year history to retain the trophy when they face Barcelona in Rotterdam on May 14, hoping their Spanish opponents offer a less relentless challenge than Liverpool.
Holding a seemingly comfortable 3-0 lead from the first leg, PSG were rattled as early as the 12th minute when Robbie Fowler lashed home an angled left-foot volley to reduce the arrears.
They then experienced a nerve-jangling final 10 minutes after Mark Wright had headed powerfully past goalkeeper Bernard Lama from a corner to give Liverpool a 2-0 lead.
That set up an even more intense last few minutes with the home fans screaming for one more goal which just would not come.

The English team, who gave themselves a mountain to climb after a woeful first leg display in Paris two weeks ago, dropped captain John Barnes and played with an adventurous four-man attack, maintaining the pressure from almost the first minute.

Even goalkeeper David James joined the attack in the final frantic minutes, heading a corner over the bar. A goal then would have eased his own recent on-field problems and taken the match into extra time, but PSG hung on.
Their Brazilian manager Ricardo was a relieved man afterwards.
"I was surprised Liverpool played with four attackers, they gave us plenty of problems throughout," he said.

"I was especially worried in the last 10 minutes after they scored their second. The ball was in the air a lot and anything could have happened. It was a very difficult game for us and I am very pleased it is over."
Liverpool battled for every single loose ball and the battle for supremacy between Stan Collymore and Bruno N'Gotty summed up the intensity of the game.

The two powerfully-built men clashed throughout and it was an early tussle that went Collymore's way which created the goal for Fowler. Collymore played the ball back into space for the young English international to strike his 31st and goal of the season.

The hard-running of Steve McManaman, the distribution of Michael Thomas and the utter conviction of the recalled Neil Ruddock all caught the eye as Liverpool relentlessly pressed forward, while PSG's heroes on the night were defenders Jimmy Algerin, N'Gotty and Paul Le Guen.

Fowler, Stig Inge Bjornebye, Collymore and Jamie Redknapp also all went close for Liverpool, while PSG's best chance fell to Patrice Loko in the second minute when he shot narrowly wide with only James to beat.
Liverpool manager Roy Evans, who said the defeat in Paris two weeks ago was Liverpool's worst performance of the season, congratulated his side for this performance.
"Obviously we had to be bold and aggresive and try to win the game. From start to finish the effort was full of passion and pride.

"It would have been a fairytale if James had scored, but it was not to be. If we had come away from Paris with a reasonable scoreline, we might have done better, but it was always going to be difficult coming back from 3-0 down. We were close, but not close enough."
